main_text.p: uit, qui hac ipsa etiam grassante perse-quutione (quatenùs coniectura assequi possum) illam orationem ad suos ciues Nazianzenos habuit, in qua non obstan-te Imperatoris sæuitia, de obedientia Principibus præstanda ita loquitur. [Subijciamur tum Deo, tum alij alijs, tam eis qui Imperium in terra gerunt; Deo quidem omnibus de causis, alij au-tem alijs, propter charitatis fœdus, Principibus denique, propter ordinem publicæque disciplinæ rationem. Nec dissi-militèr{x} Aphrates Monachus, à quo to-ta pendebat Ciuitas Antiochena, quem cùm ex Vrbe fugientem Imperatorem conspicatus esset, quò inquit, vadis? atque Aphrates modestè quidem & pru-denter: pro Imperio tuo precaturus, re-sponsit. Vbi hæc attexitur nota marginalis, in nullo non conuentu olim Christiani pro Principibus suis orarunt: quin & inui-olabiles esse Principum personas, inter alios huius ęui Doctores clarè docet Optatus Milevitanus lib. 2. contra Parmenia-num,his verbis, [Saul antequàm peccaret, vnxit meruit: post vnctionem, non leuiter offendit; hoc Deus cùm videret, propter oleum

page.notes: <note letter="x" side="right">x Niceph. ex Theod. li. II. cap. 2.</note> Damage: none visible on the text column. The word "re-sponsit" is hard to read and is copied as "re-sponsit" with [?] in the text. The printed mark after "militèr" is a raised x and is set as {x} in the text. The bracket before "Subijciamur" and the bracket before "Saul" are both as printed. The text of the last line "oleum" is right-aligned and continues onto the next page.
